findings.highlight: I’m going to take a walk.
findings.evidenceJa: ちょっと出てくる。
findings.governingReading: Shirou says only that he is going out briefly.
findings.explanation: The English invents a recreational walk and conceals that he is leaving to check on Sakura.

findings.highlight: I go up the hill tinted by the sun.
findings.evidenceJa: 夕方の坂道を上っていく。
findings.governingReading: He climbs the slope in the evening.
findings.explanation: The English adds a specific sun-tinted appearance absent from the line.

findings.highlight: Ohwell, I was just close by
findings.evidenceJa: ぁいや、なんとなく。
findings.governingReading: “Ah—no, no particular reason.” Shirou evasively corrects himself before offering the nearby excuse.
findings.explanation: The English fuses “Oh” and “well” and drops the self-correction and professed lack of a reason.

findings.highlight: My bewilderment must have been funny, as Sakura smiles.
findings.evidenceJa: 俺の慌てぶりがおかしかったのか、桜は楽しそうに微笑む。
findings.governingReading: Apparently amused by how flustered he is, Sakura smiles happily.
findings.explanation: mirror moon changes visible fluster into bewilderment and omits the pleasure in Sakura’s smile.

findings.highlight: It’s a big smile
findings.evidenceJa: その顔は本心からのもので
findings.governingReading: Her expression is heartfelt and genuine.
findings.explanation: Physical size replaces the narration’s judgment that Sakura’s smile comes from her true feelings.

findings.highlight: it doesn’t look like Shinji’s forcing her.
findings.evidenceJa: 慎二に無理やり連れ戻されたようには見えなかった。
findings.governingReading: She does not look as though Shinji forcibly made her return home.
findings.explanation: The completed coercive return becomes vague ongoing force in the present.

findings.highlight: Fujimura-sensei only told me that I should go home since my grandfather’s waiting.
findings.evidenceJa: 言われただけですから、よくは……
findings.governingReading: Sakura only knows what Fujimura told her and trails off that she does not really know the details.
findings.explanation: The English ends with the reported message and omits Sakura’s explicit epistemic limitation.

findings.highlight: it is true that Shinji hasn’t done anything to Sakura.
findings.evidenceJa: 慎二のヤツが桜に何も話していないのは本当だった。
findings.governingReading: It is true that Shinji has told Sakura nothing about the situation.
findings.explanation: A claim about withholding information becomes the much broader claim that Shinji has done nothing to Sakura.

findings.highlight: He would never involve
findings.evidenceJa: 巻き込む筈がない。
findings.governingReading: Shirou believes there is no reason to expect Shinji to involve his capable sister.
findings.explanation: “Never” hardens Shirou’s trust-based expectation into an absolute guarantee.

findings.highlight: Good.
findings.evidenceJa: 安心した。
findings.governingReading: Shirou blurts out that he is relieved.
findings.explanation: The active simultaneous line replaces his emotional relief with generic approval.

findings.highlight: about ten seconds.
findings.evidenceJa: 十数秒。
findings.governingReading: Their vacant mutual stare lasts more than ten seconds—ten-odd seconds.
findings.explanation: “About ten” permits less than ten and loses the source’s ten-plus duration.

findings.highlight: we should’ve done so earlier.
findings.evidenceJa: ……じゃあ、桜
findings.governingReading: Shirou begins, “...Then, Sakura—” before their simultaneous requests.
findings.explanation: The English deletes the unfinished address that sets up the comic overlap.

findings.highlight: I won’t be able to go to your house
findings.evidenceJa: 先輩のお家に行くのは遠慮します。
findings.governingReading: Sakura politely says she will refrain from going to Shirou’s house.
findings.explanation: Her deferential choice becomes an external inability.

findings.highlight: It’s disappointing
findings.evidenceJa: 張り合いがなくなっちゃいますけど
findings.governingReading: She will lose a source of purpose, stimulation, or something to apply herself to.
findings.explanation: The generic repeated “disappointing” loses what helping at the Emiya home contributes to Sakura’s daily life.

findings.highlight: Sakura bows
findings.evidenceJa: 最後にペコリ、とお辞儀をして
findings.governingReading: At the end Sakura gives a small, neat bow.
findings.explanation: The diminutive gesture and its place as her final response are omitted.

findings.highlight: An angry swordsman awaited me
findings.evidenceJa: 怒りながらも俺を待っていたセイバー
findings.governingReading: Saber, though angry, has waited for Shirou at the entrance.
findings.explanation: mirror moon replaces Saber’s name and identity with the masculine generic “swordsman,” while losing the concessive force of her waiting despite anger.

findings.highlight: at the entranceand I told her
findings.evidenceJa: 玄関で怒りながらも俺を待っていた
findings.governingReading: She was waiting at the entrance despite her anger.
findings.explanation: The English visibly joins “entrance” and “and,” corrupting the sentence boundary.

findings.highlight: how we eliminated the boundary field at school
findings.evidenceJa: 学校に張ってあった結界の消去
findings.governingReading: the removal of the bounded field that had been spread over the school
findings.explanation: The source report names the event without assigning its removal to a collective “we”; mirror moon supplies that agent.

findings.highlight: I don’t want her to consider him as an enemy
findings.evidenceJa: 敵と認識する事は避けたかったからだ。
findings.governingReading: Shirou himself wanted to avoid recognizing or designating Shinji as an enemy until Shinji’s intentions became clear.
findings.explanation: The English transfers the judgment to Saber, weakening Shirou’s deliberate reluctance to classify his friend as an enemy.

findings.highlight: since we were kids.
findings.evidenceJa: ガキの頃以来だな
findings.governingReading: Shirou has not had Fuji-nee’s cooking since he himself was a kid.
findings.explanation: The plural “we” also places Fuji-nee in childhood and changes their age relationship.

findings.highlight: I’m half scared and half looking forward to it.
findings.evidenceJa: 不安半分、楽しみ半分で居間に向かう。
findings.governingReading: Half anxious and half excited, he heads toward the living room.
findings.explanation: The English retains the mixed feeling but omits the action that closes the transition.

findings.highlight: it was going to turn into such a disaster
findings.evidenceJa: あのような惨劇の幕開けになろうとは
findings.governingReading: that this would become the opening curtain of such a tragedy
findings.explanation: The mock-horror theatrical image is reduced to a generic disaster.

findings.highlight: Who could have imagined
findings.evidenceJa: 誰が予測しえたであろうカ。
findings.governingReading: Who could possibly have foreseen it? The final カ is deliberately rendered in katakana.
findings.explanation: The English drops the elevated foretelling diction and the marked typographic horror cadence.
